blocks.title: Position & displacement on a number line
blocks.summary: Position is a location relative to a chosen origin. In this lesson, right is positive. Displacement is final position minus initial position: $\Delta x=x_f-x_i$. Distance adds the lengths of all parts of a journey. A negative displacement tells you a direction; it is not a negative distance.

blocks.markdown:
**Position** describes a location. **Displacement** describes a change in location.

A **scalar** has magnitude only: distance is a scalar. A **vector** has magnitude and direction: displacement is a vector. In one dimension, the sign tells you the direction.

question.prompt: A cart returns to where it started. Which statement must be true?

options.feedback: Displacement compares final and initial position. The path can still have a nonzero length.
Distance adds the lengths traveled. Returning does not erase the outward trip.

options.text: Its distance is negative on the return trip.
options.feedback: Distance is a nonnegative length. A direction can make displacement negative, not distance.

blocks.markdown: Choose right as positive. A cart starts at −2 m, travels to +4 m, then returns to +1 m.

visual.alt: Reference: start minus 2 meters, turn at plus 4 meters, finish at plus 1 meter.

blocks.work:
First segment: $|4-(-2)|=6$ m. Return segment: $|1-4|=3$ m.

Distance: $6+3=9$ m.

Displacement: $1-(-2)=+3$ m.
blocks.given: Initial: −2 m. Turn: +4 m. Final: +1 m. Model the trip on one straight number line, with right positive.
blocks.answer: Distance = 9 m. Displacement = +3 m: 3 m to the right. The return trip increases distance while reducing the final displacement.
blocks.prompt: Find the total distance and the displacement for the trip.
blocks.equation: $\Delta x=x_f-x_i$; distance = sum of segment lengths. Use the endpoints for displacement and add each segment length for distance, because the cart changes direction.

blocks.title: Distance vs. displacement on a number line · Worked Problem 01
blocks.summary: Follow the trip +2 m → +8 m → −3 m using Problem → Model → Plan → Work → Answer. Pause at 1:40, just before Work, and try the calculation. Resume to compare your method and interpret the sign.

blocks.title: Distance and displacement method
blocks.markdown:
**Problem:** Name the quantities you need.

**Model:** Choose a positive direction, label the positions, and draw every leg.

**Plan:** For distance, add the lengths of all legs: $d=|x_1-x_0|+|x_2-x_1|+\cdots$. For displacement, use only the endpoints: $\Delta x=x_f-x_i$. Use $y$ for a vertical axis.

**Work:** Substitute signed positions; take magnitudes for distance.

**Answer:** Include meters and interpret the displacement sign. Check $d\geq|\Delta x|$.

Video chapters: 0:00 Problem · 0:30 Model · 1:04 Plan · 1:40 Work · 2:20 Answer.

[Watch Worked Problem 01 on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B51oRJa9MSM) · [Worked Problems: Kinematics playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLZKwzUFM2PaM)

blocks.prompt: A student starts at +2 m, walks to a fountain at +8 m, then to a locker at −3 m. Find distance and displacement.
blocks.given: Use a straight x-axis with right positive. Mark start +2 m, turn +8 m, and finish −3 m. Draw the two legs in order.
blocks.equation: Distance adds the magnitude of each leg. Displacement compares only the endpoints: $\Delta x=x_f-x_i$.
blocks.work: First leg: $|8-2|=6$ m. Second leg: $|-3-8|=11$ m. Distance: $6+11=17$ m. Displacement: $-3-2=-5$ m.
blocks.answer: Distance = 17 m. Displacement = −5 m: the student finishes 5 m to the left of where she started. The return leg adds distance; it does not subtract distance.

blocks.prompt: A student starts at x = +1 m, walks along a straight hallway to x = +7 m, then turns and walks to x = −2 m. Choose right as positive. Find the total distance and displacement, and explain the direction of the displacement.

stageHints.model: Draw a number line. Mark +1 m as start, +7 m as the turn, and −2 m as finish. Draw one arrow for each leg.
stageHints.plan: Add the lengths of both legs for distance. For displacement, compare only the initial and final positions.
stageHints.work: Write final minus initial for each leg. Use each leg’s magnitude when adding distance, and keep meters with your values.
stageHints.answer: Report both quantities with units. Explain what the displacement sign means for your chosen positive direction.

frames.text: The total distance is ___ m. The displacement is ___ m, which means ___. They differ because ___.

blocks.note: Teacher solution — Practice 1 · A new turnaround. Model: +1 m → +7 m → −2 m; positive right. Plan: sum the magnitude of every leg for distance; Δx = xf − xi for displacement. Work: signed leg changes = +6 m, −9 m. Distance = 6 + 9 = 15 m. Displacement = (−2) − (+1) = −3 m. Answer: The student finishes 3 m left of the starting point. Adding signed leg changes gives displacement, not distance. Review the model, plan, arithmetic, units, and interpretation; a completed save alone is not evidence of correctness.

blocks.prompt: A cart starts at x = −4 m, rolls directly to x = +3 m, then returns to x = −4 m. Choose right as positive. Find distance and displacement. Explain why returning to the start does not erase the distance traveled.

stageHints.model: Show both legs, even though the initial and final positions share the same point.
stageHints.plan: Which calculation depends on the whole route? Which depends only on the endpoints?
stageHints.work: Write final minus initial for each leg. Use each leg’s magnitude when adding distance, and keep meters with your values.
stageHints.answer: Report both quantities with units. Explain what the displacement sign means for your chosen positive direction.

frames.text: The total distance is ___ m. The displacement is ___ m, which means ___. They differ because ___.

blocks.note: Teacher solution — Practice 2 · Back to the start. Model: −4 m → +3 m → −4 m; positive right. Plan: sum the magnitude of every leg for distance; Δx = xf − xi for displacement. Work: signed leg changes = +7 m, −7 m. Distance = 7 + 7 = 14 m. Displacement = (−4) − (−4) = 0 m. Answer: The displacement is zero because the endpoints coincide. There is no net direction, but both 7 m legs count toward distance. Review the model, plan, arithmetic, units, and interpretation; a completed save alone is not evidence of correctness.

blocks.prompt: A robot moves on one straight track through these positions in order: +5 m → −1 m → +2 m → −3 m. It moves directly between each listed position. Right is positive. Find its total distance and displacement. Show a model and a plan before calculating, then check that the distance is at least as large as the magnitude of the displacement.

stageHints.model: Label each stop in order and count the legs. A table or a number-line sketch can organize the route.
stageHints.plan: Choose which positions each quantity needs. Explain your choice before doing the arithmetic.
stageHints.work: Write final minus initial for each leg. Use each leg’s magnitude when adding distance, and keep meters with your values.
stageHints.answer: Report both quantities with units. Explain what the displacement sign means for your chosen positive direction.

frames.text: The total distance is ___ m. The displacement is ___ m, which means ___. They differ because ___.

blocks.note: Teacher solution — Practice 3 · Plan a longer trip. Model: +5 m → −1 m → +2 m → −3 m; positive right. Plan: sum the magnitude of every leg for distance; Δx = xf − xi for displacement. Work: signed leg changes = −6 m, +3 m, −5 m. Distance = 6 + 3 + 5 = 14 m. Displacement = (−3) − (+5) = −8 m. Answer: The robot finishes 8 m left of its start. The check is 14 m ≥ |−8 m|; changes of direction add distance without increasing the net change by the same amount. Review the model, plan, arithmetic, units, and interpretation; a completed save alone is not evidence of correctness.

blocks.prompt: A cart follows the route x = −6 m → −2 m → −5 m, moving directly between each stop. Right is positive. Find distance and displacement. Its final position is negative: does that make its total displacement negative? Use your calculation to explain.

stageHints.model: Put all three positions left of zero, then draw the motion arrows in order.
stageHints.plan: The sign of final position tells you which side of the origin it is on. To find the sign of displacement, compare final with initial position.
stageHints.work: Write final minus initial for each leg. Use each leg’s magnitude when adding distance, and keep meters with your values.
stageHints.answer: Report both quantities with units. Explain what the displacement sign means for your chosen positive direction.

frames.text: The total distance is ___ m. The displacement is ___ m, which means ___. They differ because ___.

blocks.note: Teacher solution — Practice 1 · Negative position, positive change. Model: −6 m → −2 m → −5 m; positive right. Plan: sum the magnitude of every leg for distance; Δx = xf − xi for displacement. Work: signed leg changes = +4 m, −3 m. Distance = 4 + 3 = 7 m. Displacement = (−5) − (−6) = +1 m. Answer: The final position is −5 m, but displacement is +1 m: the cart finishes 1 m to the right of where it started. Its final leg is leftward; that is different from its total displacement. Review the model, plan, arithmetic, units, and interpretation; a completed save alone is not evidence of correctness.

blocks.prompt: A lift moves directly from y = +2 m to y = −4 m, then to y = +1 m. Up is positive. Find its total distance and displacement. State the direction of the last leg and the direction of the total displacement, and explain why they differ.

stageHints.model: Turn the number line vertically. Label up as positive and mark the three positions.
stageHints.plan: Use Δy = yf − yi for the whole trip. The direction of the final leg depends on a different pair of positions.
stageHints.work: Write final minus initial for each leg. Use each leg’s magnitude when adding distance, and keep meters with your values.
stageHints.answer: Report both quantities with units. Explain what the displacement sign means for your chosen positive direction.

frames.text: The total distance is ___ m. The displacement is ___ m, which means ___. They differ because ___.

blocks.note: Teacher solution — Practice 2 · Use a vertical axis. Model: +2 m → −4 m → +1 m; positive up. Plan: sum the magnitude of every leg for distance; Δy = yf − yi for displacement. Work: signed leg changes = −6 m, +5 m. Distance = 6 + 5 = 11 m. Displacement = (+1) − (+2) = −1 m. Answer: The last leg is 5 m upward, while total displacement is −1 m (1 m down from the start). A positive final position does not imply positive total displacement. Review the model, plan, arithmetic, units, and interpretation; a completed save alone is not evidence of correctness.
